frozenFoundation.rule: V6.2.2 and the integrated Road LTL V1.2 child are immutable. V6.2.3 adds guide/knowledge only.

purpose.whatItIs: A global-neutral supply-chain, logistics and distribution reference architecture that keeps source-native frameworks, Atlas crosswalks, execution overlays, enterprise lenses, systems/objects and evidence boundaries distinguishable.
purpose.realWorld: Use the Atlas as a governed map of how supply-chain work fits together: what happens, who does it, which systems/objects/evidence are involved, which sources support the statement, and how context changes execution.
whatItIsNot: A claim that one framework contains the whole Atlas
A client-specific operating model unless client evidence is mapped
A claim that every Atlas A3/A4/A5 label is source-native

methodology.name: Preserve source-native process architecture
methodology.groundedMeaning: SCOR and APQC remain independent native frameworks. Their published semantics are shown/crosswalked rather than silently rewritten as Atlas-native taxonomy.
methodology.plainEnglish: Start with established process frameworks instead of inventing a new supply-chain language and pretending it came from an industry body.

methodology.name: Separate modelling notation from process evidence
methodology.groundedMeaning: BPMN and DMN are modelling/decision notations. They can represent workflow and decision logic later, but they are not logistics process-content evidence.
methodology.plainEnglish: A diagramming language can show a process; it does not prove that the process itself is an industry standard.

methodology.name: Add semantic/object/interoperability standards
methodology.groundedMeaning: UN/CEFACT, UN/EDIFACT, GS1 and related standards provide business-object, identity, event and message semantics within their published scope.
methodology.plainEnglish: These sources help define what the data, documents, identifiers and events mean across organizations and systems.

methodology.name: Add mode, role and legal/regulatory source packs conditionally
methodology.groundedMeaning: Mode/role/legal references are applied only within their actual mode, jurisdiction, contract, goods and carriage scope. Inclusion in the source universe never means universal applicability.
methodology.plainEnglish: A rule can be authoritative without applying to every shipment. The Atlas keeps the rule available but activates it only when the real-world context qualifies.

methodology.name: Create Atlas canonical navigation and crosswalks
methodology.groundedMeaning: Atlas domains/lenses/navigation organize the source material. Crosswalks are explicitly Atlas interpretations and may be one-to-many.
methodology.plainEnglish: The Atlas gives users one coherent way to navigate many different standards without falsely claiming the standards use the same structure.

methodology.name: Build execution children under the Page-0 parent
methodology.groundedMeaning: Detailed Road LTL A4/A5 records are Atlas child synthesis inherited from Page 0 and bounded issuer evidence. They are not claimed as source-native SCOR/APQC nodes.
methodology.plainEnglish: Page 0 is the enterprise map; LTL is a detailed operating playbook built under that map using multiple sources and explicit synthesis.

methodology.name: Separate ontology from process flow
methodology.groundedMeaning: Typed entities (state, event, decision, rule, control, action, evidence, outcome, actor, object) and their ontology relationships are governed separately from process-flow edges such as PRECEDES, REQUIRES, TRIGGERS or RECOVERS_TO.
methodology.plainEnglish: What something *is* is different from what happens *before or after* it. The Atlas keeps those two questions separate.

methodology.name: Keep provenance, claim boundaries and confidence visible
methodology.groundedMeaning: Every detailed record carries provenance/source mapping/claim boundary/confidence so users can distinguish source-native evidence, Atlas synthesis and unresolved research.
methodology.plainEnglish: The Atlas should be able to answer not only ‘what does this say?’ but also ‘where did this come from and how certain are we?’

methodology.name: Compose execution context without deleting the enterprise universe
methodology.groundedMeaning: Mode/service is the primary execution lens; role, movement, node, jurisdiction, carriage regime, condition and contract/service refine applicability. Enterprise lenses remain analytical views over the same governed universe.
methodology.plainEnglish: Choose the operating situation you care about, but do not pretend the rest of the enterprise stops existing.

methodology.name: Treat gaps as hypotheses, not conclusions
methodology.groundedMeaning: A visible failure or automation gap is not proof of root cause or value. Trace upstream/downstream dependencies, evidence, controls, frequency, materiality and economics before design.
methodology.plainEnglish: Where a problem shows up is often not where it started. Investigate before proposing automation or AI.

architectureLayers.name: Page 0 / Ecosystem
architectureLayers.meaning: Global-neutral enterprise envelope, native-framework views, canonical domains, enterprise lenses, source universe and execution-context controls.

architectureLayers.name: Source-native frameworks
architectureLayers.meaning: SCOR/APQC and other issuer material kept distinguishable from Atlas interpretation.

architectureLayers.name: Atlas crosswalks / canonical navigation
architectureLayers.meaning: One-to-many mappings and canonical navigation used to relate heterogeneous sources without claiming equivalence.

architectureLayers.name: Mode/service child
architectureLayers.meaning: Detailed execution architecture inherited from Page 0 and supported by bounded mode/issuer evidence; Road LTL V1.2 is the first completed child.

architectureLayers.name: Execution context
architectureLayers.meaning: Role, movement, node, jurisdiction, regime, conditions and contract/service refine what is active, conditional, bypassed or research-required.

architectureLayers.name: Enterprise lenses
architectureLayers.meaning: A–AA lenses connect execution to enterprise capabilities/outcomes; they do not create a second execution taxonomy.

architectureLayers.name: Client twin
architectureLayers.meaning: Client facts map onto the Atlas with explicit evidence states. Reference-only content never becomes client truth automatically.

hierarchy.plainEnglish: The map of the whole territory.

hierarchy.meaning: Governed parent process/domain boundary used by the child
hierarchy.plainEnglish: A meaningful business process area that groups detailed work.

hierarchy.meaning: Detailed execution process record in the child
hierarchy.plainEnglish: A concrete operational step, such as build a consolidation or execute a line-haul leg.

hierarchy.meaning: Execution transition components: event, states, decision, rule, control, action, evidence and outcome
hierarchy.plainEnglish: What actually happens inside an A4 step: trigger, decision, work, proof and resulting state.

ontologyTypes: What operational work is being performed?
Condition of an object/process before or after execution.
What is true before/after the work?
Occurrence that triggers or records a change.
What happened that caused the next step?
Deterministic logic constraining a decision or action.
Governance/compliance check preventing or detecting unacceptable execution.
What check keeps the process controlled?
Record proving what happened or supporting a state/decision.
What proof would an auditor/operator rely on?
What result did the step create?
Who does, owns, decides or holds custody?
What business thing is being created, changed or consumed?
System that is authoritative for a business object/state.
Which system should be trusted for this fact?
flowRelationships: PRECEDES
The source process normally occurs before the target.
This usually comes first.
FOLLOWS
The source follows the target.
This normally happens afterward.
REQUIRES
The target depends on the source/prerequisite.
You cannot validly do this without that prerequisite.
ENABLES
The source makes the target executable/available.
Completing this unlocks the next capability.
TRIGGERS
The source directly initiates the target.
This event/process starts the next one.
MAY_TRIGGER
The source can conditionally initiate the target.
This path happens only in some cases.
BRANCHES_TO
A decision/condition can take execution to another path.
The flow can split here.
ESCALATES_TO
Unresolved execution moves to an escalation path.
The issue is handed to a higher/exception route.
RECOVERS_TO
Recovery returns execution to a governed point.
After fixing the problem, the flow re-enters here.
ALTERNATIVE_TO
One path can substitute for another under a valid context.
Use one route or the other depending on conditions.
ITERATES_TO_NEXT_LEG
Execution repeats for another network leg.
The same movement pattern repeats for the next leg.
contextDimensions: Which transport/service network are we talking about?
Whose operating perspective are we taking: shipper, carrier, 3PL, 4PL, etc.?
How does freight move: direct, line-haul, hub-and-spoke, first/last mile, consolidation, etc.?
Where is the work happening: terminal, cross-dock, warehouse, DC, etc.?
Which competent authorities and local law may matter?
Does CMR/e-CMR, CIM, UPU, CMNI or another carriage regime actually apply?
Is the shipment dangerous goods, bonded, temperature-controlled, customs transit, security-controlled, etc.?
Is the service direct carriage, forwarder-arranged, managed logistics, postal or private CEP?
Which enterprise capability/outcome do we want to analyze without changing the execution taxonomy?

stateVocabulary.meaning: The process is active in the current composed execution graph.
stateVocabulary.plainEnglish: This step is part of the current scenario/context.

stateVocabulary.meaning: A valid selected context intentionally skips the process.
stateVocabulary.plainEnglish: The step still belongs to LTL knowledge, but this configuration takes a route that does not use it.

stateVocabulary.meaning: The item is a direct dependency or directly relevant to the current focus.
stateVocabulary.plainEnglish: This is one of the nearby things you should look at to understand the selected item.

stateVocabulary.meaning: Governed Road LTL knowledge that remains in the model but is outside the current focus/direct dependency set.
stateVocabulary.plainEnglish: It is still part of the overall LTL operating model, just not directly involved in the thing you are tracing right now.

stateVocabulary.meaning: The source supports model construction/claims within a bounded scope.
stateVocabulary.plainEnglish: We can use this source to support the model, but that does not mean the source is legally operative for this shipment.

stateVocabulary.meaning: The source exists in the governed universe but current context does not activate it.
stateVocabulary.plainEnglish: This rule/standard may matter in another situation, but not based on what is currently selected.

stateVocabulary.meaning: Context suggests the source may apply, but provision-level/legal scope still requires resolution.
stateVocabulary.plainEnglish: This looks potentially relevant, but do not treat it as operative until the actual scope is confirmed.

stateVocabulary.meaning: The implementation context has explicitly adopted/resolved the source as operative for the relevant scope.
stateVocabulary.plainEnglish: For this governed context, this source has been confirmed as the rule/standard we are actually using.

stateVocabulary.meaning: Current governed evidence is insufficient for the claimed execution detail.
stateVocabulary.plainEnglish: The Atlas deliberately stops here rather than inventing detail.

stateVocabulary.meaning: Useful source/crosswalk coverage exists, but implementation detail remains unresolved.
stateVocabulary.plainEnglish: We know enough to navigate/analyze the area, but not enough to pretend we have a complete operating playbook.

provenanceClasses.name: SOURCE-NATIVE
provenanceClasses.meaning: Content represented as belonging to the issuer's own framework/standard vocabulary.
provenanceClasses.plainEnglish: This label/structure genuinely comes from the named source framework.

provenanceClasses.name: SOURCE-NATIVE CROSSWALK
provenanceClasses.meaning: Atlas mapping from a canonical/enterprise construct to source-native nodes while preserving source identity.
provenanceClasses.plainEnglish: The Atlas links its navigation to the framework; it does not claim the framework uses Atlas labels.

provenanceClasses.name: REFERENCE-DERIVED CROSSWALK
provenanceClasses.meaning: Atlas analytical mapping derived from reference sources where no single source-native hierarchy is claimed.
provenanceClasses.plainEnglish: Multiple references support the idea, but the final grouping is an Atlas interpretation.

provenanceClasses.name: ATLAS ANALYTICAL / CONTROL CONSTRUCT
provenanceClasses.meaning: Atlas-created analytical/control lens, explicitly not claimed as source-native taxonomy.
provenanceClasses.plainEnglish: This is a useful way to analyze the enterprise, but it is our analytical construct rather than an industry framework node.

provenanceClasses.name: ATLAS CHILD SYNTHESIS
provenanceClasses.meaning: Detailed child execution model inherited from Page 0 and bounded issuer evidence.
provenanceClasses.plainEnglish: The detailed operating flow is assembled by the Atlas from its parent structure and multiple authoritative sources; no single framework is claimed to own the whole flow.

provenanceClasses.name: RUNTIME / PRESENTATION STATE
provenanceClasses.meaning: UI/composition/trace state generated by the Atlas runtime; not source evidence.
provenanceClasses.plainEnglish: This is how the interface is showing relevance or status right now, not an industry classification.

sourceArchitecture.role: Native process/reference semantics and cross-enterprise process structure.
Represent workflow and decision logic; not process-content evidence.
Business objects, identifiers, events, messages and cross-party semantics.
Mode-, network- or role-bounded operating/document/data evidence.
Operative only when actual legal, geographic, goods, contract and carriage scope resolves.
Enterprise-control boundaries, data quality, governance and enabling controls.

page0Walkthrough: Overview
Start here. Choose Mode / Service first; refine role, movement, node and legal/service context only when known.
Planned navigator
Shows the governed future-page universe. Coming soon means the destination is planned but unsupported execution detail has not been invented.
Ecosystem atlas
Shows canonical enterprise domains and their relationships across the whole supply-chain/logistics envelope.
Source-native models
Inspect SCOR/APQC in their own identities and see Atlas crosswalks without collapsing framework boundaries.
Enterprise coverage
Use A–AA lenses to examine planning, commercial, finance, claims, risk, controls, etc. over the same execution universe.
Operating roles
Change perspective/responsibility without assuming one role owns the whole chain.
Execution overlays
Refine mode/service, movement/node and context-specific execution applicability.
Systems & exchanges
See systems, authoritative objects, interfaces and exchange relationships.
L3–L5 contract
Understand the minimum structure every detailed child must inherit: process, event/state, decision/rule/control, action, evidence, outcome, actors, systems, objects and sources.
White-space discovery
Trace top-down outcomes and bottom-up execution friction before declaring a gap or designing AI/automation.
Sources
Audit issuer, version/status, applicability, role, claim supported/not-supported and source relationship state.
ltlWalkthrough: Six real-world stages: Commit & qualify; Ready & collect; Origin node; Network movement; Destination & delivery; Evidence & settlement.
Read the process label, phase/path, before-state, trigger/event, decision/rule/control/clock, action, evidence, after-state and outcome.
Distinguish performer, owner, decision authority, custody and exception owner instead of using one generic 'owner'.
Distinguish producer/consumer/interface from the system authoritative for the business object.
Focus one item and inspect direct governed dependencies. Grey/other knowledge remains part of the LTL universe unless the composed context truly bypasses it.
Read each process claim boundary and source relationship state before treating a framework/regulation as applicable.

Switch between End-to-End, Physical, Information, Financial, Controls, Actors, Systems, Documents, Data, Exceptions, Enterprise Dependencies and Sources without changing the underlying process universe.
clientEvidenceStates: Operational/client evidence supports the fact, but explicit human confirmation may still be pending.
Credible external/public evidence supports it; not the same as client confirmation.
Reasoned hypothesis from known facts; must never auto-promote.
Atlas says the component exists in the reference model; client-specific reality is unknown.
No reliable client-specific fact is known.

explanationPolicy.ambiguityRule: If exact ID/current clicked UI context does not resolve the term and two or more valid namespaces remain, ask a clarification question instead of choosing by keyword score.
explanationPolicy.llmRole: The LLM explains grounded Atlas evidence in practical language and examples. It does not determine provenance, applicability, client truth or taxonomy by itself.
explanationPolicy.examplesRule: Gemini may use generic logistics examples to explain a grounded concept, but must label them as illustrative and must not turn them into Atlas/client facts.

governance: Frozen V6.2.2 and Road LTL V1.2 content cannot be mutated by intelligence.
Source-native, crosswalk, Atlas synthesis and runtime state must remain distinguishable.
A source must never be used beyond its stated claim boundary.
Legal/regulatory applicability is conditional and provision/scope dependent.
Unknown and reference-only client areas must not be filled by model knowledge.
Atlas corrections are advisory; administrator manually creates a new governed Atlas source release.
If classification is ambiguous, clarification precedes explanation.
Plain-English explanation must not erase the technical definition/provenance underneath it.
